clue.text: A persistent one never finishes a sentence!

definitions.text: A persistent one never finishes a sentence!

parts.words: A persistent one never finishes a sentence!
parts.note: a 'sentence' here is a prison term, not a line of words; someone who keeps escaping from jail never serves one to the end

explanation.surface: A grammar joke about a chatterbox who never completes what they are saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual prison escaper never completes a jail term, the sense of sentence the clue hides.

clue.text: Deny a saying is wrong

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says a well-known proverb is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wrong' tells you to rearrange the seven letters of A SAYING.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or refuse to accept, a formal synonym for deny.

clue.text: A possessive type

parts.note: reads like a jealous, clinging person, but means simply someone who possesses things

explanation.definitionFit: A person who has property literally possesses it, so is a possessive type in the plain sense.

clue.text: Retract support on quiet deal that's been arranged

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: something arranged has been put in order, so the letters of deal are reordered

explanation.surface: A backer withdraws their support from a business deal once it has been agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's been arranged' turns DEAL into EDAL; 'on' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpedal is to reverse a stated position, an idiom for withdrawing what one said.

clue.text: A misshapen nose ages

indicators.note: a misshapen thing has been bent out of its proper form, so the letters of nose are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked nose makes someone look older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misshapen' rearranges NOSE; 'ages' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Eons are immensely long stretches of time, as ages are in the loose sense.

clue.text: Observe inner need when profoundly involved

indicators.note: the word need is placed inner, that is inside the synonym for observe

parts.note: to keep a rule or festival is to observe it

explanation.surface: Notice a deep inner longing when someone is emotionally caught up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inner' reads like an adjective for need, but it is the container signal; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up to the knees in something is an idiom for being thoroughly caught up in it.

clue.text: Lover of Shakespeare

parts.note: not a fan of the playwright's works but a young man in love in one of his tragedies

explanation.definitionFit: The Verona youth who falls for Juliet is the playwright's most famous ardent suitor.

clue.text: Tells of twinges after gym lesson

indicators.note: the twinges come after the gym lesson, so their word follows

parts.note: PE is physical education, the school gym class
twinges are small pains, aches

explanation.surface: A pupil complains of little pains following a PE class.
explanation.walkthrough: To peach is old slang for informing on someone; 'Tells of' looks like describing but means betrays.
explanation.definitionFit: To peach on an accomplice is a dated slang way to inform on or betray them.

clue.text: Union gets a nice settlement after all

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the word all

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a settlement is a sorting-out, so the letters of a nice are settled into a new order

explanation.surface: A trade union is pleased to reach a good deal at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlement' rearranges A NICE into IANCE; 'gets' is a link and 'after all' looks like the idiom 'in the end'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a formal joining of parties for a shared purpose, a synonym of union.

clue.text: In no way, one says, could this be to blame

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the phrase for in no way sounds like a single word

parts.note: in no way means in no sense

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that this quality could not possibly be at fault.
explanation.walkthrough: IN NO SENSE, said aloud, gives the answer; the definition is the question 'could this be to blame?', to which the answer itself replies 'in no way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being free of guilt is exactly the state of which one would ask whether it could be blameworthy.

clue.text: The toast of former opera-goers

parts.note: both a famous old soprano adored by audiences and the thin crisp toast named after her

explanation.definitionFit: Nellie Melba, the Australian soprano, was celebrated by audiences of her day, and Melba toast bears her name.

clue.text: Fights are things dogs enjoy

definitions.meaning: leftover bits of food thrown to a dog

explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is informally a scrap, and leftover morsels of food are scraps given to pets.

clue.text: Warn a pretty girl about a Scotsman

indicators.note: the slang word for pretty girl goes about, around, the Scots word

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
mon is the Scots form of man

explanation.surface: Caution an attractive young woman who is with a man from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Dish is old slang for an attractive person; the second 'a' is a link, since only the first gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish is to reprove or caution someone, close in sense to warn.

clue.text: Even barren ground does, if one fights them enough

definitions.text: Even barren ground does, if one fights them enough

parts.words: Even barren ground does, if one fights them enough
parts.note: poor soil produces crops when worked hard, and opponents give in when fought long enough: two senses of one verb

explanation.surface: A stubborn farmer is told that persistence pays off with even the worst land.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to produce a crop and to surrender, covering the soil and the beaten foe.

clue.text: Rise late, perhaps, but still be the first

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Even a late riser can still be first to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges RISE LATE; 'but still be' joins the pieces and makes the paradox.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliest means coming before all others in time, which is being the first.

clue.text: It seems to me to be the old way of saying it

definitions.text: the old way of saying it
definitions.meaning: an archaic one-word form used in older English such as Shakespeare

explanation.definitionFit: The archaic expression literally means 'it seems to me', a usage found in Elizabethan English.

clue.text: Hired vehicle that always comes with a backseat driver

definitions.text: Hired vehicle that always comes with a backseat driver

parts.words: Hired vehicle that always comes with a backseat driver
parts.note: a backseat driver is normally a nagging passenger; here the driver literally sits up behind the passengers

explanation.definitionFit: In the Victorian two-wheeled carriage for hire, the coachman sat high at the back.

clue.text: Changes locks

definitions.meaning: locks of hair, here hairpieces of detached hair

explanation.definitionFit: Exchanges are switches, and bunches of false hair worn to add bulk are also called switches.

clue.text: Legislation that went against the grain

definitions.text: Legislation that went against the grain

parts.words: Legislation that went against the grain
parts.note: against the grain usually means contrary to inclination, but here means laws aimed at imported cereal

explanation.definitionFit: The 19th-century British tariffs on imported wheat restricted the cereal trade until repealed in 1846.

clue.text: Small companies start collections for pets

indicators.note: the companies piece comes at the start, before the collections

parts.note: COS is the shortened, small form of companies
sets are collections of things

explanation.surface: Little firms begin putting together sets of things for animal lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pets' looks like a noun, animals, but is the verb meaning pampers.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper and indulge, which is what petting someone means.

clue.text: A letter reportedly gets an extension

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard rather than read

parts.note: the letter X is spoken as 'ex', so a letter is 'an ex'

explanation.surface: A piece of post brings news that a deadline has been extended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' means said aloud: 'an X' sounds like the answer; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building added on to a larger one, a form of extension.

clue.text: One who helps another to a seat

definitions.text: One who helps another to a seat

parts.words: One who helps another to a seat
parts.note: suggests an usher showing someone to a chair, but means a voter who sends a candidate into parliament

explanation.definitionFit: A voter helps put a candidate into a parliamentary constituency, known in Britain as a seat.

clue.text: What winter sportsmen may need to reach their peak

definitions.text: What winter sportsmen may need to reach their peak

parts.words: What winter sportsmen may need to reach their peak
parts.note: reach their peak sounds like hitting top form but means getting up to the mountain top

explanation.definitionFit: Skiers ride a cable-drawn chair or tow up the slope to its summit.

clue.text: Did little after I'd made the running

indicators.note: the word for made the running comes after I'd

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
to make the running is to set the pace, to lead

explanation.surface: Someone did nothing much once they had set the pace.
explanation.walkthrough: To make the running is a racing idiom for setting the pace in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to pass time doing nothing useful, so having idled means one did little.

clue.text: Not one to run

definitions.meaning: two of something, rather than one
as in 'on the ...', at a running pace

explanation.definitionFit: Twice as many is not one, and 'at the double' is a military order to move at a run.

clue.text: Burnt out with stress

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: Someone is exhausted by pressure at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BURNT; 'with' is a link. The definition is stress in the sense of pressure or impact.
explanation.definitionFit: The brunt is the chief force or pressure of something, as in bearing the brunt of an attack.

clue.text: Brother to uncle Remus

parts.note: the American folk tales narrated by Uncle Remus use a dialect form of brother before animal names

explanation.definitionFit: Joel Chandler Harris's Uncle Remus tales feature Rabbit and Fox titled with this Southern dialect word for brother.

clue.text: Support for a board of education

definitions.text: Support for a board of education

parts.words: Support for a board of education
parts.note: board of education suggests a council committee, but means a classroom blackboard on its stand

explanation.definitionFit: A wooden three-legged stand holds up a blackboard or painting.

clue.text: Difficult to make love other than on grass

parts.note: hard means difficult
in the old sense, to court is to woo

explanation.surface: Lovemaking is awkward unless done away from the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make love' is used in its old meaning, to woo; the definition refers to a tennis surface that is not grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is played on grass, clay or tarmac-type surfaces; the last kind is the non-grass option named here.

clue.text: Marketing agent for a car engine component

definitions.meaning: a wholesaler who supplies goods to shops
the part that sends high voltage to each spark plug in turn

explanation.definitionFit: A wholesaler supplies goods to retailers, and the ignition part routes current to each cylinder's spark plug.
